main_text.l: Sed Babylonij repentè alias atq; aliàs gentes hostiliter invaserunt & oppresserunt. Ergo idem erit eorum quoque fatum. Utitur autem Dominus ἐρωτήματι[?] ut torporem excutiat ijs, qui ista absurda & impossibilia esse putabant.

l.i: In subitis rerum conuersionibus, infelices esse seculi huius filios, contra vero felices Dei filios.

main_text.l: Multum dissimiles esse fideles & infideles, cum subitae rerum conuersiones, tempestatis cuiusdam instar, ingruunt, o-ratio Domini Dei nostri docet, etsi in ea tantum huius seculi hominum mentio fiat.
Infelices sunt infideles, sive in magnis illis rerum humanarum mutationibus e-mergant, sive mergantur: ut ex hisce colligi potest.
1. Quòd neutrum providentia Dei eve-nire, vere statuunt.
2. Quòd in rebus secundis vehementer luxuriant eorum animi.

page.notes: Printed text runs to the foot of the page with the catchword "stafi" at the right; the catchword reading is uncertain. The Greek word after "Dominus" (ἐρωτήματι?) and the Greek phrase in point 3 (ἀλλὰ τῇ φιλανθρωπίᾳ?) are doubtful and marked [?]. Long s rendered as plain s throughout; printed "etfi", "ipfis", "fubitis", "conuerfionibus" are normalised accordingly. Printed "fiue" and "hifce" are read as "sive" and "hisce"; the ligature in "s" forms is kept as plain s. Possible printing errors: "eve-nire" hyphen position at line end is as printed.
